title: Grip, timing & direction
summary: Find the balance point, free up your grip, then learn the four relationships that organize double staff spinning.

setup.grip: Hold the balance mark between thumb and index finger. Let the other fingers relax.
setup.stance: Start standing comfortably with room for each end of both staves. The stance shown in the guide is a neutral practice suggestion.
setup.plane: Start in front of your body. Track the same marked end on each staff.

moves.name: Find the balance point
moves.description: The middle mark identifies the staff's center of gravity. Use it as your reference for a balanced grip.
moves.grip: Place thumb and index finger at the middle mark.
moves.stance: Hold one staff in front of you while locating its center.
moves.focus: Equal length on each side of the hand.

steps.title: Locate
steps.body: Find the center mark, then check that the two sides balance.

steps.title: Hold
steps.body: Keep the grip centered as you begin turning the staff.

moves.name: Thumb–index pinch
moves.description: Use a light drumstick-like hold, with the staff between the first index joint and thumb pad, or resting in the web between them.
moves.grip: Thumb pad against index finger; other fingers remain available rather than clamped.
moves.stance: Keep your hand where you can watch the contact point.
moves.focus: Let the shaft rotate without squeezing it in a closed fist.

steps.title: Pinch
steps.body: Support the balance point between thumb and index finger.

steps.title: Release tension
steps.body: Let the remaining fingers move away while preserving control.

moves.name: Open the grip in both directions
moves.description: Move between the index-supported position and the open-hand position with the shaft resting in the thumb–index web.
moves.grip: Allow the contact surface to change as the staff rolls through the hand.
moves.stance: Try one hand, then both, with space around your fingertips.
moves.focus: Follow the grip change instead of forcing a wrist twist.

steps.title: Index support
steps.body: Turn until the shaft lies along the extended index finger, with the thumb lightly supporting its side.

steps.title: Web support
steps.body: Turn the other way into the open-hand position, supporting the shaft in the thumb–index web.

steps.title: Reverse
steps.body: Move gently back and forth through both positions, then try the other hand.

moves.name: Together time · same direction
moves.description: Follow matching staff ends as they go around together in the same direction.
moves.grip: Keep a consistent thumb-end reference on both staves.
moves.stance: Give both hands room to trace matching circles.
moves.focus: The marked ends reach each part of their circles together.

steps.title: Match
steps.body: Start the marked ends at the same point in the cycle.

steps.title: Travel
steps.body: Move both clockwise, or both counterclockwise, maintaining that relationship.

moves.name: Split time · same direction
moves.description: Keep the direction the same while separating the marked ends by half a turn.
moves.grip: Continue tracking the same end of each staff.
moves.stance: Let the hands occupy opposite sides of their circular paths.
moves.focus: When one marked end is high, the other is low.

steps.title: Separate
steps.body: Place the marked ends half a cycle apart.

steps.title: Match speed
steps.body: Move in the same direction without closing that gap.

moves.name: Together time · opposite directions
moves.description: Move in opposite directions, meeting at the top and bottom of the circle.
moves.grip: Use the marked ends to identify the meeting points.
moves.stance: Mirror the two arm movements across your centerline.
moves.focus: Top and bottom are together; left and right are apart.

steps.title: Meet high
steps.body: Bring the marked ends toward the top from opposite sides.

steps.title: Open
steps.body: Move apart to the sides and meet again at the bottom.

moves.name: Split time · opposite directions
moves.description: Reverse the meeting axis: the marked ends now meet at the sides and separate at the top and bottom.
moves.stance: Start with one hand high and the other low.
moves.focus: The two side positions are the shared points.

steps.title: Separate vertically
steps.body: Place one marked end high and the other low.

steps.title: Meet sideways
steps.body: Move in opposite directions toward the same side, then continue around.

moves.name: Link the four timing modes
moves.description: Use a shared position to reverse one hand and enter a new timing relationship. The source demonstrates a complete cycle through all four.
moves.grip: Maintain the reference ends as you change direction.
moves.stance: Keep the pattern small enough to pause clearly at each shared point.
moves.focus: Change direction at a matching position, rather than jumping a hand across the circle.

steps.title: Together same → together opposite
steps.body: Reverse one hand when both reference ends meet at the top or bottom.

steps.title: Together opposite → split same
steps.body: Reverse one hand when the ends are separated across the sides.

steps.title: Split same → split opposite
steps.body: Reverse at the high–low alignment.

steps.title: Split opposite → together same
steps.body: Reverse at a shared side position.

pitfalls: Double staffs have two ends. Track the thumb end consistently or a half-turn can look deceptively identical.
The source verbally slips on some timing names; the definitions here use the demonstrated meeting points.

evidence.observation: Close grip uses thumb pad and index joint.
Index-supported extreme shown close to the camera.
Open hand supports shaft in the thumb-index web.

limitations: The body guide is schematic, not a reconstruction of the instructor's joints.

title: Hip & shoulder reels
summary: Send the staff through front and rear spaces, then combine hip and shoulder reels in each timing relationship.

setup.grip: Use the centered thumb–index grip and identify the thumb and pinky ends.
setup.stance: Stand with room behind your hips and shoulders; start with one staff.
setup.plane: Reels use both front and rear spaces. Use the side view and source close-ups for depth.

moves.name: Single-staff hip reel
moves.description: The thumb end traces the front circle while the pinky end passes behind the body.
moves.grip: Let the centered grip open as the pinky end goes behind you.
moves.stance: Work beside the hip, keeping the elbow available for the rear passage.
moves.focus: Pinky behind at the waist; thumb in front.

steps.title: Thumb up
steps.body: Begin with the thumb end up and the pinky end down.

steps.title: Pinky behind
steps.body: Send the pinky end behind the back as the thumb end extends to the side.

steps.title: Pass the elbow
steps.body: Let the pinky end pass behind the elbow, then bring the thumb end across the front of the waist.

steps.title: Return
steps.body: Arrive thumb-up again and connect the positions smoothly.

moves.name: Single-staff shoulder reel
moves.description: At shoulder height, the roles reverse: thumb end behind, pinky end in front.
moves.grip: Preserve the centered grip as the thumb end clears the shoulder.
moves.stance: Allow room behind the shoulder and around the head.
moves.focus: Thumb behind at the shoulder; pinky in front.

steps.title: Lift the pattern
steps.body: Move the staff to shoulder height.

steps.title: Thumb behind
steps.body: Pass the thumb end behind the shoulder while the pinky end circles in front.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.body: Connect the front and rear portions into a continuous reel.

moves.name: Link hip and shoulder reels
moves.description: Use the end that belongs behind the body at the destination to lead the change in height.
moves.grip: Let the supporting contact shift without losing the center mark.
moves.stance: Move the hand between waist and shoulder height.
moves.focus: Thumb leads upward; pinky leads downward.

steps.title: Rise
steps.body: Lead from hip to shoulder with the thumb end.

steps.title: Descend
steps.body: Lead from shoulder to hip with the pinky end.

steps.title: Reverse
steps.body: Try the same height change in the other rotation direction.

moves.name: Together-same reels
moves.description: Match the ends and their timing, then carry both reels from hips to shoulders and back.
moves.grip: Keep the two thumb ends matched throughout the height changes.
moves.stance: Use matching hip or shoulder levels initially.
moves.focus: Both staves repeat the same movement together.

steps.title: At the hips
steps.body: Run both hip reels together.

steps.title: At the shoulders
steps.body: Raise both using the thumb ends to lead.

steps.title: Connect
steps.body: Move between the two heights without changing the timing.

moves.name: Together-opposite reels
moves.description: Opposite rotation produces the eggbeater-like relationship demonstrated at the hips and shoulders.
moves.grip: Keep the ends identifiable while the shafts cross in projection.
moves.stance: Make room for the two separate planes, especially around the head.
moves.focus: Meeting timing stays together while directions oppose.

steps.title: At the hips
steps.body: Make the two hip reels mirror each other.

steps.title: Raise
steps.body: Explore the shoulder-level version with controlled head clearance.

steps.title: Mix levels
steps.body: Pause at either height before returning to the other.

moves.name: Split-opposite reels
moves.description: One thumb end goes up as the other goes down. Explore the same level and alternating hip–shoulder levels.
moves.grip: Track the opposed thumb ends rather than the whole shafts.
moves.stance: Let one hand work high while the other works low.
moves.focus: Thumb down at the shoulder; pinky up near the hip.

steps.title: Offset
steps.body: Start one thumb end high and the other low.

steps.title: Change height
steps.body: Switch which hand works at the hips and which works at the shoulders.

steps.title: Keep opposition
steps.body: Maintain opposite direction while linking the levels.

moves.name: Split-opposite reels with turns
moves.description: Drex breaks the turn into a high–low swap on one side, a half-turn, and the opposite swap.
moves.stance: Turn toward one side, switch the high and low hands, then turn 180 degrees.
moves.focus: Keep the hand-level change readable before adding the body turn.

steps.title: Face right
steps.body: Put the left thumb down behind the shoulder and right pinky up beside the hip.

steps.title: Switch levels
steps.body: Bring the left pinky up at the waist and right thumb down at the shoulder.

steps.title: Turn
steps.body: Turn to the other side and reverse the high–low arrangement.

moves.name: Split-same hip reels
moves.description: Both staves rotate in the same direction with half-cycle spacing. One passes through the gap between the other staff and the torso.
moves.grip: Keep a light grip so each staff can pass through its own front–rear space.
moves.stance: Maintain a deliberate gap in front of the torso.

steps.title: Offset
steps.body: Set the two reels half a cycle apart in the same direction.

steps.title: Make a passage
steps.body: Leave a gap between one staff and your front so the other can pass.

steps.title: Repeat the checkpoint
steps.body: Return to thumbs at center and pinkies behind on successive cycles.

pitfalls: The end that passes behind changes between hip and shoulder reels.
The source presents split-same at the hips and describes the shoulder version as unfinished practice, not a fully taught variation.

evidence.observation: Turn drill separates level switching from the 180 degree turn.

limitations: Reel animation is a depth schematic; source close-ups are the reference for the exact grip and clearance.
